Gold price needs a dovish Fed or renewed debasement fears to reverse its downtrend – Bank of America
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Investment demand in gold-backed exchange-traded funds has been resilient in the face of persistent inflation, higher bond yields and a stronger U.S. dollar; however, one bank remains cautious on the precious metal as physical demand remains weak, particularly in key global markets. ( Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.) In their latest precious metals note, commodity analysts at Bank of America said that despite steady investment demand, they are not ready to reassess their outlook for gold prices, as they expect prices will be unable to hold above $4,000 an ounce over the next three months. “We remain cautious near-term as the macro environment remains challenging: we have an average 4Q26 forecast of $4,000/oz, but then expect prices to average $4,813 in CY27,” the analysts said in the report published Monday.

Gold ETF demand defies rising bond yields as investors pour $31 billion into record third quarter – WGC
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold faces headwinds as persistent inflation pressures support higher interest rates, driving bond yields and the U.S. dollar higher. However, investors continue to see value in the precious metal, as demand for gold-backed exchange-traded funds remained positive through September. In its latest monthly ETF report, the World Gold Council (WGC) said that 67.3 tonnes of gold, valued at nearly $10 billion, flowed into global ETFs last month. The analysts added that September’s strong performance lifted third-quarter inflows to a record $31 billion, with European- and North American-listed funds leading demand. “During Q3, global gold ETFs’ total AUM rose 9%, while collective holdings grew by 211t. At the country level, the record Q3 inflow was led by the US, followed by an impressive contribution from UK-listed funds. The UK recorded its strongest quarter on record, helping Europe achieve the same milestone at the regional level,” the analysts said.

Gold prices struggle to hold early gains as U.S. dollar nears 18-month high, bond yields remain elevated - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) – The gold market is struggling to maintain its recent recovery as persistent inflation pressures, elevated bond yields and a U.S. dollar trading near an 18-month high continue to create significant headwinds for the precious metal ahead of another critical week of economic data. Gold prices started the week with modest gains, briefly trading above $4,200 an ounce during the Asian session; however, bullish momentum has faded as investors remain reluctant to take significant positions ahead of Wednesday's U.S. Consumer Price Index report. Spot gold was last quoted around $4,156.20 an ounce ahead of the North American trading session, down nearly 1% on the day. The precious metal has been unable to build on last week's recovery after prices briefly fell below $4,100 an ounce. Despite the recent buying momentum, gold remains well below its August highs as investors continue to assess the implications of tighter monetary policy and stubborn inflation.

Norway fines Microsoft subsidiary for sharing Grindr user data
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Norway's data protection authority Monday slapped a 92 million kroner (8.6 million euros) fine on Microsoft subsidiary Xandr for sharing user data from dating app Grindr. Xandr, an online advertising company, is accused of processing and then transmitting data from Grindr users to a real-time advertising bidding system, where it may have been shared with potentially thousands of companies to enable them to display targeted ads.
